title: Pedir vs Preguntar: Asking For vs Asking About
seo_title: Pedir vs Preguntar: Asking For vs Asking About
meta_description: Pedir vs preguntar: both mean “to ask”, but one asks for things and the other asks questions. Rules, examples, real dialogues, common mistakes and a quiz.
excerpt: One asks for things, the other asks questions. Here’s how to never mix them up again.

body_html:
Pedir vs preguntar is one of the first confusing pairs English speakers meet, because English uses one verb, “to ask”, for both. In Spanish, the difference is simple once you see it: pedir means to ask for something (an object, a favour, an action), and preguntar means to ask a question or ask about something. Get this right and you will instantly sound more natural in restaurants, at work and with friends.

Quick answer
  • Pedir = to ask for, request, order: pedir la cuenta, pedir un favor.
  • Preguntar = to ask a question, ask for information: preguntar la hora.
  • Shortcut: if the answer is a thing or action, use pedir; if it is information, use preguntar.
  • “To ask a question” is hacer una pregunta, never preguntar una pregunta.
{{toc}}

Pedir vs preguntar: the core rule

PedirPreguntar
Meaningto ask for, to request, to orderto ask (a question), to inquire
You want…something or someone to do somethinginformation
ExamplePedí un café. I ordered a coffee.Pregunté el precio. I asked the price.
With peopleLe pedí ayuda. I asked him for help.Le pregunté su nombre. I asked her name.

The RAE dictionary defines pedir as asking someone to give or do something, while preguntar is asking someone for information. That is the whole distinction in one sentence.

When to use pedir

  • Ordering: ¿Qué vas a pedir? What are you going to order?
  • Requesting objects: Le pedí el coche a mi padre. I asked my dad for the car.
  • Favours and help: ¿Te puedo pedir un favor? Can I ask you a favour?
  • Apologising: Te pido perdón. I apologise / I ask your forgiveness.
  • Borrowing: Pedí prestado un libro. I borrowed a book.
  • Asking someone to do something: Te pido que llegues a tiempo. I’m asking you to arrive on time.

Notice the last example: pedir que is followed by the subjunctive (llegues), because you are requesting an action.

When to use preguntar

  • Questions: Me preguntó dónde vivo. She asked me where I live.
  • Yes/no questions with si: Pregúntale si quiere venir. Ask him if he wants to come.
  • Asking about someone: Tu madre preguntó por ti. Your mother asked about you.
  • Asking oneself: Me pregunto qué pasará. I wonder what will happen.

Preguntarse (to wonder) is a lovely structure that English speakers often miss.

{{image:2}}

A mental shortcut

Imagine the answer you hope to get. If someone could hand it to you or do it for you (a coffee, a favour, the bill), it is pedir. If the answer is words or facts (a name, a time, a yes or no), it is preguntar. Asking for directions is a good test: Le pregunté cómo llegar a la estación (information), but Le pedí que me acompañara (an action).

Conjugation note

Pedir is a stem-changing verb (e → i): pido, pides, pide, pedimos, pedís, piden; past pedí, pediste, pidió, pidieron. Preguntar is completely regular: pregunto, preguntas, pregunta…

{{book:the-mind-lies}}

Real conversations

At a restaurant

  • Waiter: ¿Ya saben qué van a pedir? (Do you know what you’re going to order?)
  • You: Sí, yo pido la paella. Una pregunta: ¿lleva marisco? (Yes, I’ll have the paella. A question: does it have seafood?)
  • Waiter: Sí, lleva gambas y mejillones. (Yes, prawns and mussels.)
  • You: Perfecto. ¿Y nos puede traer agua, por favor? (Perfect. And could you bring us water, please?)

At work

  • A: Ana me preguntó si terminamos el informe. (Ana asked me if we finished the report.)
  • B: Dile que necesitamos más tiempo. Le voy a pedir dos días más. (Tell her we need more time. I’m going to ask her for two more days.)

Common mistakes

IncorrectCorrectWhy
Le pregunté un favor.Le pedí un favor.A favour is requested, not asked about
Voy a preguntar la cuenta.Voy a pedir la cuenta.You want the bill itself
Quiero preguntar una pregunta.Quiero hacer una pregunta.Spanish says “make a question”
Me pidió dónde vivo.Me preguntó dónde vivo.Where you live is information
Pedir para dineroPedir dineroPedir takes a direct object, no “for”

That last one is a classic calque from English “ask for”. In Spanish, the “for” is already inside pedir.

{{image:3}}

Useful expressions

  • pedir la mano: to ask for someone’s hand in marriage
  • pedir cita: to make an appointment (Spain)
  • pedir disculpas: to apologise
  • preguntar por alguien: to ask after someone
  • ¿Puedo hacerte una pregunta?: Can I ask you a question?

If you liked this pair, try {{link:llevar-vs-traer|llevar vs traer}} and {{link:saber-vs-conocer|saber vs conocer}}, or browse {{link:spanish-confusing-words|my complete list of Spanish confusing words}}. Asking for things politely is also part of everyday situations like {{link:writing-emails-in-spanish|writing emails in Spanish}}.

{{quiz}}

Final thoughts

Pedir vs preguntar comes down to one question: do you want something, or do you want to know something? Ask for things with pedir, ask about things with preguntar, and the confusion disappears.

faq.q: What is the difference between pedir and preguntar?
faq.a: Pedir means to ask for or request something (an object, a favour, an action). Preguntar means to ask a question or ask for information.

faq.q: How do you say “to ask a question” in Spanish?
faq.a: Hacer una pregunta. Saying preguntar una pregunta is a common learner mistake.

faq.q: Is ordering food pedir or preguntar?
faq.a: Pedir. ¿Qué vas a pedir? means “What are you going to order?”

questions.q: Voy a ___ la cuenta. (I’m going to ask for the bill.)
questions.explain: You want the bill itself, so it is pedir.

questions.q: Le ___ a qué hora abre la tienda. (I asked him what time the shop opens.)
questions.explain: The opening time is information: preguntar.

questions.q: ¿Te puedo ___ un favor? (Can I ask you a favour?)
questions.explain: A favour is something requested: pedir.

questions.q: Which is correct for “Can I ask you a question?”
Mi abuela siempre ___ por ti. (My grandmother always asks about you.)
questions.explain: Preguntar por alguien means to ask after someone.
